item.title: Top 5 Stories This Morning: John Waters Keynote, Christmas Village Returning, Tool Library, and more.
item.description: Last week, we shared news about the German-style Christmas Village at the Inner Harbor, John Waters' keynote address at The Association of Writers & Writing Programs (AWP) 2026 Conference and Bookfair in Baltimore, plans for a Falls Road property, and preview of the Station North Tool Library's upcoming Fix-It Fair.

item.title: Baltimore’s Connector Program Makes Jewish Community Accessible
item.description: When Dante Barboy decided to become a Community Connector last fall, he had a simple vision: create spaces where young Jewish adults could connect over everyday, fun activities. “I wanted to build community with other Jewish people through everyday activities,” explains Dante. “It could be a concert, movie, or happy hour. The list goes on.” […]

item.title: What’s next for Maryland’s redistricting plan?
item.description: Despite a push to get the General Assembly to approve a mid-cycle redistricting plan, the effort appears to have failed. Proponents say that’s not so.

item.title: Carroll County Government holds sale for compost bins, rain barrels
item.description: Carroll County Government Office of Recycling Operations is holding a compost bin and rain barrel sale through April 5.

item.title: Howard County renters get stronger protections against eviction with new legislation
item.description: Howard County Executive Calvin Ball signed legislation that will protect renters from evictions and strengthen nonprofits in the county.

item.title: As Congress debates agricultural trade, Maryland farmers feel the impact
item.description: Lawmakers questioned a USDA under secretary in an oversight hearing about trade policy and the growing U.S. agricultural trade deficit. Two Maryland farmers say their reality goes beyond the walls of Washington.

item.title: Vintage team apparel means steady income for these Baltimore sellers
item.description: Team sportwear has become a niche for vintage sellers, and Baltimore entrepreneurs are cashing in. Teams have been inspired to recreate retro apparel to benefit from the trend.

item.title: Howard County moves to make affordable housing and homeownership a reality for more residents
item.description: The focus of two recent initiatives by Howard County Executive Calvin Ball is adding and maintaining affordable housing.

item.title: Barnes & Noble to open bookstore at proposed Lutherville Station
item.description: Barnes & Noble plans to open a store in late 2026 or early 2027 as part of Lutherville Station, a transit-oriented development proposed off Ridgely Road.
